source_refs.note: Exercise 11.1, Question 7: book page 290 (Q1-Q8). The book prints no answers for Unit 11; every answer here is ours.

blocks.prompt: 7 (i) Find the domain and range of the following vector-valued function: \(\mathbf{r}(t) = \sqrt{t}\,\hat{i} + \ln t\,\hat{j}\)
blocks.explanation:
Domain: components ke domains ka intersection (11.2.1).
Range: tamam output vectors \(\mathbf{r}(t)\) ka set (11.2). In vectors ke sire (tips) ek curve banate hain, jo hum \(t\) khatam kar ke dhoondte hain.
Rule: \(\sqrt{t}\) ke liye \(t \ge 0\), \(\ln t\) ke liye \(t > 0\).
Plan: pehle domain, phir \(x = \sqrt{t}\), \(y = \ln t\) rakh kar \(t\) ko hata denge aur dekhenge ke curve ka kaun sa hissa milta hai.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\mathbf{r}(t) = \sqrt{t}\,\hat{i} + \ln t\,\hat{j}\).
Maloom karna: domain aur range.
Tareeqa: domain = jahan har component defined ho (11.2.1 ke Step 1-2). Range = tamam outputs \(\langle x(t), y(t)\rangle\) ka set; \(y\) ko \(x\) ki shakal mein likhne se pata chalta hai ke kaun se points milte hain.

Har component ka domain
\(\sqrt{t}\): \(t \ge 0\) chahiye, domain \([0, \infty)\).
\(\ln t\): \(t > 0\) chahiye, domain \((0, \infty)\).
\[[0, \infty) \cap (0, \infty) = (0, \infty)\]
Kyun: \(t = 0\) par \(\sqrt{0}\) to ban jata hai magar \(\ln 0\) defined nahin, is liye zero nikal gaya. Dono ka mushtarka hissa sirf positive numbers hain.
Yaad rakhein: root ke andar \(\ge 0\), log ke andar \(> 0\), aur denominator \(\ne 0\): domain ke yahi teen bare rules hain.

\(t\) khatam karein
\[x = \sqrt{t} \Rightarrow t = x^2,\ x > 0\]
\[y = \ln t = \ln(x^2) = 2\ln x\]
Kyun: dono components \(t\) ke zariye jure hue hain. Pehli equation se \(t\) nikal kar doosri mein rakha, to \(x\) aur \(y\) ka seedha rishta mil gaya: yahi woh curve hai jis par har output parta hai. Log ka rule \(\ln x^2 = 2\ln x\) (jab \(x > 0\)).
Dhyan dein: \(\ln(x^2) = 2\ln x\) sirf \(x > 0\) par sahi hai, aur yahan \(x = \sqrt{t}\) hamesha positive hai, is liye koi masla nahin.

Kaun se points milte hain?
Jab \(t\) poore \((0, \infty)\) mein chalta hai to \(x = \sqrt{t}\) har positive value leta hai, is liye curve \(y = 2\ln x\), \(x > 0\), ka har point milta hai.
\[\text{Range} = \{(x, y) : x > 0,\ y = 2\ln x\}\]
Component-wise: \(x(t)\) poora \((0, \infty)\), aur \(y(t)\) tamam real values.
Kyun: \(\sqrt{t}\) barhta hi jata hai aur koi had nahin; \(\ln t\) \(-\infty\) se \(\infty\) tak jata hai.
Dhyan dein: range ek curve hai, poora ilaqa nahin.
Figure mein dekhein: curve \(y\)-axis ke qareeb bohat neeche se aata hai aur \((1, 0)\) se guzar kar aahista aahista oopar jata hai.

Tasdeeq
\(t = 1\): \(\mathbf{r}(1) = \hat{i} + 0\,\hat{j}\), aur \(2\ln 1 = 0\) \(\checkmark\).
\(t = 4\): \(\mathbf{r}(4) = 2\hat{i} + \ln 4\,\hat{j}\), aur \(2\ln 2 = \ln 4\) \(\checkmark\).
Kyun: misaal ke taur par \((1, 5)\) output nahin hai: \(x = 1\) ka matlab \(t = 1\), aur phir \(y = \ln 1 = 0\), 5 nahin. Is liye "\(x > 0\), \(y\) koi bhi real" poora jawab nahin; \(x\) aur \(y\) aazad nahin, \(t\) se bandhe hue hain.
blocks.final_answer: Domain: \((0, \infty)\). Range: \(\{(x, y) : x > 0,\ y = 2\ln x\}\), yani poora curve \(y = 2\ln x\) (yahan \(x \in (0, \infty)\), \(y \in \mathbb{R}\)).

answer_figure.alt: Graph of the curve y = 2 ln x for x greater than 0, rising from far below near the y-axis through (1, 0). Marked points: t = 1/4 at (1/2, -1.39), t = 1 at (1, 0), t = 4 at (2, 1.39), t = 9 at (3, 2.20). Arrows show the direction of increasing t.
answer_figure.caption: The tip of r(t) = √t i + ln t j traces the whole curve y = 2 ln x, x > 0 (our drawing)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Vector function ki range: kitab (11.2) ise tamam output vectors \(\mathbf{r}(t)\) ka set kehti hai. In vectors ke sire ek curve banate hain, is liye hum range ko curve ki equation(s) se bayan karte hain, jo \(t\) khatam kar ke milti hain. Har component ka interval bhi saath diya hai, lekin akele woh intervals ek bara set bayan karte hain, asal range nahin.

blocks.prompt: 7 (ii) Find the domain and range of the following vector-valued function: \(\mathbf{r}(t) = \cos(t)\,\hat{i} + \sin(t)\,\hat{j}\)
blocks.explanation:
Domain: jahan \(\cos t\) aur \(\sin t\) dono defined hon.
Range: output vectors ka set; identity \(\cos^2 t + \sin^2 t = 1\) \(t\) ko khatam kar deti hai.
Yeh wahi circle hai jo Question 2 mein bana tha, bas radius 1 aur \(\omega = 1\).
Plan: pehle domain, phir components ko square kar ke jama karenge.
Yaad rakhein: range ek shakal (curve) hai, sirf intervals nahin.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\mathbf{r}(t) = \cos t\,\hat{i} + \sin t\,\hat{j}\).
Maloom karna: domain aur range.
Tareeqa: components se domain; range ke liye \(\cos^2 t + \sin^2 t = 1\) se \(t\) khatam karna, phir dekhna ke kaun se points milte hain.

Domain
\(\cos t\) aur \(\sin t\) har real \(t\) par defined hain.
\[\text{Domain} = \mathbb{R} = (-\infty, \infty)\]
Kyun: \(\mathbb{R}\) aur \(\mathbb{R}\) ka intersection \(\mathbb{R}\) hi hai; koi pabandi nahin.

\(t\) khatam karein
\[x = \cos t,\quad y = \sin t\]
\[x^2 + y^2 = \cos^2 t + \sin^2 t = 1\]
Kyun: square kar ke jama karne se Pythagorean identity lagti hai aur \(t\) gayab ho jata hai. Har output us circle par hai jis ka centre \(O\) aur radius 1 hai (unit circle).

Kaun se points milte hain?
Jab \(t\) \(0\) se \(2\pi\) tak jata hai to \((\cos t, \sin t)\) poore circle ka ek chakkar lagata hai (phir dohrata hai).
\[\text{Range} = \{(x, y) : x^2 + y^2 = 1\}\]
Component-wise: \(x, y \in [-1, 1]\); aur har \(t\) par \(|\mathbf{r}(t)| = 1\), yani sab outputs unit vectors hain.
Kyun: unit circle ka har point kisi angle \(\theta\) ke liye \((\cos\theta, \sin\theta)\) hota hai, is liye koi point nahin chhootta.
Figure mein teeron (arrows) se dekhein ke \(t\) barhne par point anticlockwise chalta hai.

Tasdeeq
\(\mathbf{r}(0) = \hat{i}\), \(\mathbf{r}(\frac{\pi}{2}) = \hat{j}\), \(\mathbf{r}(\pi) = -\hat{i}\): sab unit circle par \(\checkmark\).
Kyun: vector \(\langle 1, 1\rangle\) ke dono components \([-1, 1]\) mein hain magar yeh range mein nahin, kyunke \(1^2 + 1^2 = 2 \ne 1\). Is liye sirf "\(x, y \in [-1, 1]\)" likhna range nahin; asal range circle hai, poora square nahin.
blocks.final_answer: Domain: \(\mathbb{R}\). Range: \(\{(x, y) : x^2 + y^2 = 1\}\), yani unit circle (centre \(O\), radius 1); yahan \(x, y \in [-1, 1]\).

answer_figure.alt: Unit circle x squared plus y squared equals 1 with centre at the origin. Points t = 0 at (1, 0), t = pi/2 at (0, 1), t = pi at (-1, 0), t = 3pi/2 at (0, -1); arrows show anticlockwise motion.
answer_figure.caption: The tip of r(t) = cos t i + sin t j goes round the unit circle (our drawing)

blocks.prompt: 7 (iii) Find the domain and range of the following vector-valued function: \(\mathbf{r}(t) = t\,\hat{i} + t^2\,\hat{j} + e^t\,\hat{k}\)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh 3D vector function hai: domain teeno components se, aur range space mein ek curve.
Yahan \(x = t\) hai, is liye \(t\) khatam karna bohat aasan hai: bas \(t\) ki jagah \(x\) likh dein.
Rule: polynomial aur \(e^t\) har real \(t\) par defined hain.
Plan: domain; phir \(y\) aur \(z\) ko \(x\) ki shakal mein likhenge.
Yaad rahe: 3D curve ke liye \(x\), \(y\), \(z\) teeno ka rishta likhna hota hai.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\mathbf{r}(t) = t\,\hat{i} + t^2\,\hat{j} + e^t\,\hat{k}\).
Maloom karna: domain aur range.
Tareeqa: domain = components ke domains ka intersection; range = outputs \(\langle t, t^2, e^t\rangle\) ka set, jise \(t\) khatam kar ke bayan karte hain.

Domain
\(t\), \(t^2\) aur \(e^t\) har real \(t\) par defined hain.
\[\text{Domain} = \mathbb{R}\]
Kyun: polynomials aur exponential function par koi pabandi nahin; na denominator hai, na root, na log.
Is liye domain ka hissa aasan hai; asal kaam range mein hai.

\(t\) khatam karein
\[x = t,\quad y = t^2,\quad z = e^t\]
\[y = x^2,\quad z = e^x\]
Kyun: \(t = x\) hai, is liye har output \(\langle x, x^2, e^x\rangle\) ban jata hai. 3D mein ek curve ke liye do equations chahiye hoti hain, aur yahan do mil gayin.

Kaun se points milte hain?
\(x = t\) har real value leta hai, is liye range poora curve hai:
\[\{(x, y, z) : y = x^2,\ z = e^x,\ x \in \mathbb{R}\}\]
Component-wise: \(x \in \mathbb{R}\), \(y \in [0, \infty)\), \(z \in (0, \infty)\).
Kyun: \(t^2\) kabhi negative nahin aur \(e^t\) hamesha positive. Yeh curve \(xy\)-plane ki parabola \(y = x^2\) ke theek oopar hai, aur hamesha us plane se oopar rehta hai (jaise parabola ki deewar par chadhti bel).
Dhyan dein: \(z\) ki range \((0, \infty)\) hai, \([0, \infty)\) nahin; \(e^t\) zero kabhi nahin hota.

Tasdeeq
\(\mathbf{r}(0) = 0\,\hat{i} + 0\,\hat{j} + 1\,\hat{k}\): \(y = 0^2\), \(z = e^0 = 1\) \(\checkmark\).
\(\mathbf{r}(1) = \hat{i} + \hat{j} + e\,\hat{k}\): \(y = 1^2\), \(z = e^1\) \(\checkmark\).
Kyun: donon points dono equations poori karte hain, is liye curve sahi hai.
blocks.final_answer: Domain: \(\mathbb{R}\). Range: \(\{(x, y, z) : y = x^2,\ z = e^x,\ x \in \mathbb{R}\} = \{\langle t, t^2, e^t\rangle : t \in \mathbb{R}\}\); yahan \(x \in \mathbb{R}\), \(y \in [0, \infty)\), \(z \in (0, \infty)\).

blocks.prompt: 7 (iv) Find the domain and range of the following vector-valued function: \(\mathbf{r}(t) = \sin(t)\,\hat{i} + \cos(t)\,\hat{j} + t\,\hat{k}\)
blocks.explanation:
Yeh 3D function kitab ke helix wale Example 3 (11.3.1) jaisa hai.
\(\sin^2 t + \cos^2 t = 1\) \(x\) aur \(y\) ko jorta hai; \(z = t\) batata hai ke curve kaise oopar uthta hai.
Plan: pehle domain; phir \(t\) khatam kar ke curve ko pehchanenge.
Yeh Question 4 ke spiral (drone) jaisa hi raasta hai.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\mathbf{r}(t) = \sin t\,\hat{i} + \cos t\,\hat{j} + t\,\hat{k}\).
Maloom karna: domain aur range.
Tareeqa: teeno components se domain; range ke liye \(t\) khatam karna (Pythagorean identity aur \(z = t\)).

Domain
\(\sin t\), \(\cos t\) aur \(t\) har real \(t\) par defined hain.
\[\text{Domain} = \mathbb{R}\]
Kyun: kisi component par koi pabandi nahin.
Is liye yahan bhi asal kaam range mein hai.

\(t\) khatam karein
\[x = \sin t,\quad y = \cos t,\quad z = t\]
\[x^2 + y^2 = \sin^2 t + \cos^2 t = 1\]
\[x = \sin z,\quad y = \cos z\]
Kyun: har output us cylinder (belan) par hai jis ka radius 1 hai aur jo \(z\)-axis ke gird hai. Aur \(z = t\) hai, is liye \(z\) maloom ho to \(x\) aur \(y\) bhi tay ho jate hain.
Socheiye: agar sirf \(x^2 + y^2 = 1\) likhte to poora cylinder aa jata; \(x = \sin z\), \(y = \cos z\) us cylinder par sirf ek lakeer (helix) chunte hain.

Kaun se points milte hain?
\(t\) barhne par point \(z\)-axis ke gird ghoomta hai aur har poore chakkar mein \(2\pi\) oopar uthta hai: yeh circular helix hai (spring ya seerhi jaisi shakal). \(z = t\) har real value leta hai, is liye helix oopar neeche dono taraf be-had chalta hai.
\[\text{Range} = \{(\sin z, \cos z, z) : z \in \mathbb{R}\}\]
Component-wise: \(x, y \in [-1, 1]\), \(z \in \mathbb{R}\).
Kyun: har \(z\) se bilkul ek point \((\sin z, \cos z, z)\) banta hai.

Tasdeeq
\(\mathbf{r}(0) = 0\,\hat{i} + \hat{j} + 0\,\hat{k}\): \(0^2 + 1^2 = 1\) \(\checkmark\).
\(\mathbf{r}(\frac{\pi}{2}) = \hat{i} + 0\,\hat{j} + \frac{\pi}{2}\,\hat{k}\): \(1^2 + 0^2 = 1\) \(\checkmark\).
Kyun: kitab ke Example 3 (\(\langle\cos t, \sin t, t\rangle\)) ki tarah yeh bhi helix hai; farq sirf itna hai ke yeh \((0, 1, 0)\) se shuru hota hai aur doosri taraf ghoomta hai.
Dhyan dein: yahan \(\hat{i}\) ke saath \(\sin\) aur \(\hat{j}\) ke saath \(\cos\) hai; ulta mat parhiye.
blocks.final_answer: Domain: \(\mathbb{R}\). Range: \(\{(\sin z, \cos z, z) : z \in \mathbb{R}\}\), cylinder \(x^2 + y^2 = 1\) par circular helix; yahan \(x, y \in [-1, 1]\), \(z \in \mathbb{R}\).
